title: Fixed V Trough and Pierced Register Bookbinding Cradle
description: One newly authored complete empty static bookbinding-punching-cradle-inspired tool. Two whole thick sloping cheek boards form an open V bed with a real full-length central separation below the register. Two complete broad V-notched end feet support both boards and leave the middle underside open. One full raised rear stop closes only the far end. A single continuous narrow register strip bridges the lower inner cheek shoulders and contains seven genuine octagonal through apertures, with complete hole walls and material bridges between openings. The central empty under-bed route is clear beneath every register hole, not a black line painted on a filled support. Every section, end-stop contour, shoulder and perforated-strip coordinate is new. Unlike the V book scanner there is no broad ground slab, blank book, imaging arch, camera head or optical system; the low empty split bed and piercing-clearance/register relation is original together, not a stripped scanner. Unlike a sewing frame there are no tall shoulder posts, bored overhead crosshead, vertical support cords or blank text block. Six complete closed editable meshes, four opaque constant PBR roles, metres native Z up and whole horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. One whole independent model zero scenes; boards and guide are not separate counted assets. Generic unmarked fixed craft-tool appearance, not a copied product, template or construction plan. No book, paper, needle, awl or sharp working tool included. The register is fixed and the small shoulder/support overlaps are static visual contacts, not removable joints or fitted manufacture. No actual puncturing, hole-spacing standard, paper alignment accuracy, binding result, tool fit, user handling, material strength, load, stability, manufacture or safety capability made or verified. No rig, animation or interaction.
